summary.text: Terry Johnson, D.O., represents Ohio's 14th Senate District, which includes Clermont, Brown, Adams, and Scioto counties; he was appointed to the Senate in 2019 and is serving his second full term. He is a retired physician and former four-term State Representative who chairs the Armed Services, Veterans Affairs and Public Safety Committee.

paragraphs.text: Johnson graduated summa cum laude from Ohio University in 1985 with a bachelor's degree in history and graduated from its College of Osteopathic Medicine in 1991, then practiced as a family physician in southern Ohio for nearly three decades.

He was commissioned into the Ohio Army National Guard while a fourth-year medical student, deployed overseas multiple times including two tours in Iraq, and ended his military career in 2011 as the Army Guard's State Surgeon.
Johnson served as Scioto County Coroner from 2002 to 2010 and was then elected to represent Ohio's 89th House District.
With Rep. Dave Burke he authored House Bill 93, the "Anti-Pill Mill Bill," signed into law in May 2011, and he sponsored House Bill 170 in 2013 to expand access to naloxone.
In the Senate he sponsored Senate Bill 157 on infants born alive after a failed abortion and Senate Bill 215, which established Constitutional Carry in Ohio.
He lives in Scioto County with his wife, Jennifer, a pharmacist, and has four adult sons and three grandchildren.
